questions.def: "Too" means excessively; "very" is for gradable adjectives.
questions.question: This coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it yet.

questions.def: "So" is used with "that" to indicate a high degree.
questions.question: The news was ___ shocking that I couldn't speak.

questions.def: "Delicious" is ungradable, so no modifiers are needed.
questions.question: The cake was ___. We ate it all.

questions.def: "Absolutely" modifies ungradable adjectives like "certain".
questions.question: I am ___ certain that he will arrive on time.

questions.def: "Utterly" emphasizes the extreme degree of "exhausted".
questions.question: She was ___ exhausted after the marathon.

questions.def: "Freezing" is ungradable, so no modifiers are normally needed.
questions.question: It's ___ outside. Wear a coat!

questions.def: "Confusing" is gradable and commonly uses "very".
questions.question: His explanation was ___ confusing. I didn't understand.

questions.def: "Interesting" is gradable, use "not very" for negative.
questions.question: The film was ___ interesting, I nearly fell asleep.

questions.def: "Unique" is ungradable; avoid "a bit unique".
questions.question: She is a bit unique, which makes her special.

questions.def: "Terrified" is ungradable, so no modifiers are needed.
questions.question: I was ___ of the dark.

questions.def: "Extremely" is used to modify gradable adjectives.
questions.question: The task was ___ difficult. It took hours.

questions.def: "Virtually" implies near fluency, common with ungradable adjectives.
questions.question: He is ___ fluent in French.

questions.def: "Furious" is ungradable, so it doesn't need a modifier.
questions.question: She was ___ about the delay.

questions.def: "Perfectly" emphasizes the completeness of "clear".
questions.question: The instructions were ___ clear and easy to follow.

questions.def: "Highly" is used to emphasize the severity of "critical".
questions.question: The situation is ___ critical.

questions.def: "Hilarious" is ungradable, so no modifiers are needed.
questions.question: The comedian was ___.

questions.def: "Deeply" is used to express strong gratitude.
questions.question: I felt ___ grateful for their help.

questions.def: "Largely" indicates a significant degree of success.
questions.question: The experiment was ___ successful.

questions.def: "Devastated" is ungradable, so no modifiers are needed.
questions.question: She was ___ by the news.

questions.def: "Quite" can modify gradable adjectives like "complicated".
questions.question: The situation is ___ complicated.

questions.def: "Heavily" indicates a significant degree of involvement.
questions.question: He was ___ involved in the project.

questions.def: "Astonished" is ungradable, so it doesn't need a modifier.
questions.question: We were ___ by the performance.

questions.def: "Talented" is gradable, so it uses "a very".
questions.question: She is ___ talented musician.

questions.def: "Remarkably" is used to emphasize the high degree of accuracy.
questions.question: The data is ___ accurate.

questions.def: Terrifying is ungradable, so it takes 'absolutely', not gradable modifiers.
questions.question: The news was absolutely ___.

questions.def: 'Incredibly' modifies ungradable adjectives like 'delicious'.
questions.question: This cake is ___ delicious.

questions.def: Exhausted is often considered ungradable; 'absolutely exhausted' is better.
questions.question: She felt very exhausted after the long flight.

questions.def: Cold is gradable, so it combines better with 'quite' than ungradable modifiers.
questions.question: The weather is ___ today.

questions.def: 'Absolutely' emphasizes the ungradable adjective 'angry'.
questions.question: He was ___ angry about the situation.

questions.def: 'Very' is suitable for the gradable adjective 'funny'.
questions.question: The movie was ___ funny.
